taxonomic_note: Accepted species and Texas-native at state scale.
look_here_first: Start with leaf size, bark, and ripe fruit: much larger leaves than Texas persimmon, dark blocky/checkered mature bark, and yellow-orange to reddish ripe fruit rather than black.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis is the only qualifying target-zone county retained in the latest review. Williamson is documented in older evidence but is outside the project target-county list; cultivated/rootstock records are excluded.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification.

best_field_traits: leaves much larger than Diospyros texana
larger yellow-orange to reddish ripe fruit
morphology_keys.comparison_training: D. texana has smaller thick leaves, pale smooth peeling bark, and black fruit.
morphology_keys.field_comparison: Mature bark deeply checkered/blackish; leaves normally larger (approx. 3.5–8 cm in USDA description) and often pointed; ripe berries yellowish-orange to reddish; calyx persists (often 4 broad lobes). Texas persimmon usually smaller blunt leaves and smooth gray bark with ripe black berry.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Large leaves plus dark blocky bark plus orange/red fruit versus small leaves, pale peeling bark, and black fruit.
